title: The geometric stalks of a constructible sheaf of modules are finite
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring, and $\mathcal F$ a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], an object of $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then for every geometric point $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ [def-weil-geometric-point] the stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar t}$ of the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] is a finite set; in particular, with the $\Lambda$-module structure induced by the $\Lambda$-module structures of the groups $\mathcal F(U)$, it is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module.

source.place: Etale Cohomology, proof of Lemma 095N (lemma-category-constructible-modules, line 12412 ff.): 'every stalk F_x is a finite type Lambda-module'; from Definition 03RU (definition-finite-locally-constant) and Definition 03RW (definition-constructible) with Lemma 03Q1 (lemma-stalk-pullback: stalk of an inverse image)

proof.text: Unpack the constructibility witness S. Since its strata cover T, the image of the unique point of Spec Omega belongs to a stratum k. Rewrite membership using range_immersion to choose z in S.domain k above that image.
Install the immersion instance of S.immersion k. Apply fieldPoint_factorsThrough_immersion to z and s to obtain s' : Spec Omega -> S.domain k with s' followed by S.immersion k equal to s.

Apply the first equivalence of finite_locally_constant_module_values_iff to the finite-value trivialization of the pullback G supplied by constructibility. Its IsFiniteSheaf field gives ConcreteCategory.IsFinitelyGenerated for the module stalk of G at s'.

Apply the existing module-valued Etale.upperStarCompSheafFiberIso to the immersion and s', then ConcreteCategory.IsFinitelyGenerated.of_iso. Rewrite s' followed by the immersion as s. This works directly in ModuleCat, so no passage to the underlying abelian sheaf or germ compatibility is needed.

Convert concrete finite generation to Module.Finite using ModuleCat.isFinitelyGenerated_iff. Mathlib Module.finite_of_finite gives a finite underlying set over the finite ring Lambda. Return both conclusions.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against 095N/03RU/03RW: correct). Proof in five steps: the geometric point lies over a point of some stratum T_k = iota_k(Z_k); it factors through the immersion iota_k (new node lem-weil-pbc-field-point-factors-through-immersion: residue fields are preserved by immersions, so Spec(Omega) -> T lifts, Stacks 01IO/01HK/01J9/01L7); the stalk of iota_k^{-1}F at the lift is the stalk of F at t-bar (lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ, 03Q1); iota_k^{-1}F is finite locally constant with finite values, so its geometric stalks are finite (lem-weil-pbc-finite-locally-constant-module-values (1)=>(2)), the module stalk and the abelian stalk having the same underlying set (filtered colimits of modules are computed on elements: lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered, lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise); a finite module is finitely generated.
